A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continuous speculative decoding study and include Appendices A–H. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original speed measurements, MAR image-quality evaluations, component ablations, DDIM experiments and qualitative generation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds acceptance-criterion measurements, xAR and Harmon quality evaluations, and additional qualitative ablations and failure cases.

M1.justification: The operational procedure is retained. v2 Equation 8 and Algorithm 1 already use separate aligned denoising paths, the covariance-factor-weighted final Gaussian density ratio, token pre-filling and rejection sampling. v3 explicitly identifies this criterion as an approximation but does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds Harmon evaluation on MSCOCO, MJHQ and GenEval, extending coverage to explicit text-image alignment, counting, colors, spatial relationships and attribute binding (Tables 6–7). v2 already evaluated Harmon speed, but contained none of these benchmark evaluations. ImageNet coverage remains.

E2.justification: v3 Table 5 introduces standalone xAR-L as a quality comparator; xAR-L was absent from v2's comparisons. Existing MAR references and the masked-generation comparison remain. Newly cited methods such as BiLD and Medusa are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce CLIPScore and GenEval scoring, xAR-L model pairings, and a three-way acceptance-criterion diagnostic using 10,000 samples at draft length 4 (Appendix A.1). Existing batch sizes, resolutions, hardware and 50,000-image FID/IS protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds the exact-versus-approximate criterion diagnostic (Table 1), image-quality ablations for trajectory alignment and pre-filling (Figures 10–11), and explicit failure/success cases (Appendix G.7, Figure 14). These extend v2's acceptance-rate and distance analyses to approximation behavior, visible artifacts and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten evaluation runs for FID/IS in Appendix D and describe reporting means and standard deviations. The added xAR results follow this existing practice. No new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance testing or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Original speedup, MAR quality and appendix numerical tables are retained, while substantial results are added. v3 Table 1 reports a shared-path ratio of 5.33×10^-23 with 0% acceptance. Tables 5–7 add xAR and Harmon quality results; for example, Harmon target-only versus speculative decoding scores are 8.39 versus 8.38 MSCOCO FID and 0.76 versus 0.75 overall GenEval.

T1.justification: v3 distinguishes joint trajectory densities from token marginal densities and explicitly defines the two-path surrogate. New Appendix A.1 adds Taylor-based bias analysis and an entropy/KL argument assuming higher draft-model entropy. v2 Appendix A.3's distribution-preservation proof is removed, while the proximity and rejection-sampling derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly identify an approximate acceptance criterion as a contribution. v2's introduction claimed provable target-distribution preservation; v3 replaces that account with approximation and bias reduction. The over-2× acceleration and maintained image-quality claims remain, although the conclusion still retains distribution-preservation wording.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that the approximate criterion lacks the original unbiasedness guarantee and attributes unaligned-generation artifacts to this bias (Sections 3.2 and 4.3). Alignment and pre-filling are now interpreted as protecting image quality as well as acceptance. Appendix G.7 develops the earlier texture/rejection observation into a draft-capacity failure explanation.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit CSpD code-repository link supplied in v2's abstract. Most implementation documentation, including official checkpoints, xAR's k=1 setting and A100 hardware, remains unchanged in Appendix D. The PDFs establish removal of the access information, not a change in repository availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds BiLD, Medusa and Smart Parallel Auto-Correct Decoding when discussing relaxed acceptance and target-model fine-tuning. New evaluation citations cover COCO, Playground v2.5, CLIPScore and GenEval. The principal positioning as an extension beyond discrete visual speculative decoding remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around the approximate criterion. The method exposition and proof appendix are reorganized to distinguish marginal, shared-path and two-path probabilities. Experimental prose is revised, and author/affiliation text and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a narrower conference layout with different typography, running headers, table-caption placement and extensive figure/table repositioning. It adds Tables 1 and 5–7 and Figures 10, 11 and 14. Earlier diagrams, plots and qualitative image grids are retained and reformatted rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency about the implemented approximation and adds useful xAR/Harmon quality validation, artifact ablations and failure examples. The gain is limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Section 3.2 acknowledges bias, while the conclusion and Appendix G.5 still imply distribution-preserving or theoretically guaranteed behavior. Removal of the code-access link also weakens reproducibility documentation.
